prediction.rationale: Persistent downtrend: 8 of 10 sessions closed lower, closes sliding from 2973.81 to 2887.05, the lowest close of the window and -3.5% off the 3008.38 peak. On 20260803 the index broke the 2881.5-2885.2 support shelf with a -1.23% drop to a new period low (2873.56) and closed near the session low. Three gap-up opens (0727, 0729, 0731) all faded to negative closes, showing rallies are being sold into. Volume on the breakdown (56.9M) sits below the 63.0M ten-day average with no capitulation spike, so there is no exhaustion/reversal signal, only fading participation. Price is ~0.96% below MA5 (2915.0) and ~1.9% below MA10 (2942.5); next supports are the 2850 psychological level and the 52-week low zone near 2779.60 (per Sohu quote page), resistance at 2912-2932. Supplementary news confirms weakness: SSE50 daily -0.52% and E Fund SSE50 ETF (510100) the largest decliner among peers (https://cj.sina.cn/articles/view/7935425109/1d8fcfa5502001kz40?from=finance), indicating continued large-cap outflows. Expect moderate follow-through weakness rather than another -1% cascade given shrinking volume and short-term oversold readings.
prediction.market_analysis: Under this view, SSE50 heavyweights keep dragging the broad market: the SSE Composite and CSI 300 likely stay soft, with index-weighted sectors — banks, insurance, brokers, liquor/consumer staples, and large-cap industrials — continuing to de-risk amid ETF outflows. Defensive rotation favors dividend/low-volatility names and bonds, while small-cap growth and thematic stocks may decouple and outperform as capital leaves mega-caps. Downside path is a test of 2850 and then the yearly-low zone near 2780; tactically, a gap-up open that fades (as on 0727/0729/0731) would confirm sellers still control the tape, whereas a high-volume reversal back above 2932 would negate the bearish bias and open a rebound toward 2950-2960. Watch for policy-support headlines, which are the main risk to this bearish stance given deeply oversold short-term readings.

prediction.rationale: Close 7079.78 sits mid-range of the 10-day band (6841.75-7302.45) after the +2.53% rebound on 0731 and a doji-like +0.06% hold on 0803 (close above open, low 7042.89 defended above the 6897/6841 double-bottom support zone). Range compressed to ~75pts (~1.1%) from ~147pts (~2.1%) and volume contracted to 233M shares from 283M — a low-volume consolidation rather than distribution; notably, up-day volume (0731: 283M, 0729: 271M) has exceeded preceding down-day volume since 0730, hinting at mild accumulation. Net drift over the window is +1.6% with 6 up vs 4 down sessions, though rallies have been repeatedly sold at the 7118-7132 supply zone (0730 high 7121.52, 0803 high 7118.10), capping upside. Supplementary news notes July's pullback in previously strong tech-growth names with style-rebalancing expectations rising (https://www.moomoo.com/hans/news/post/75864289), which supports rotation flows into laggards — a tailwind for the small-cap-heavy CSI 1000. Lean: modest continuation higher into resistance, low conviction given the whipsaw regime.
prediction.market_analysis: Under this view, CSI 1000 pushes back into the 7118-7132 supply zone; a break above it opens 7218-7228 (0731 high / 0727 close). Broad-market implication is stabilization after July's tech-led drawdown, with breadth improving as institutional money rotates out of crowded high-beta growth leaders into laggard small/mid caps — favorable for diversified small-cap exposure and for value, consumption and cyclical sectors catching rotation bids, while formerly dominant tech-growth names likely consolidate sideways. Invalidation: another rejection at ~7130 in a market that has alternated sharp down days after rallies would point to a retest of 6900-6841 support, favoring defensive positioning and caution on leveraged small-cap bets. Position sizing should remain moderate given the persistent ±2-3% daily swings.

prediction.rationale: The window opened with a +4.81% surge on 7/21 (close 14264.29 on the ten sessions' heaviest volume, 329.6M shares) followed by a -5.7% washout to 13448.29, but downside momentum is fading: 8/03's -0.96% was the mildest decline of the whole pullback, and its low (13407.99) held well above the double-tested 13068.56/13267.64 support shelf, producing a higher low versus the 7/30 close (13285.80). Daily ranges compressed from ~550 pts (7/30) to ~163 pts (8/03), a volatility-exhaustion pattern that typically precedes a directional leg. Volume skews toward accumulation: up days averaged ~262M shares vs ~240M on down days; 7/31's +2.21% advance printed 283.5M shares (a six-session high) while the 8/03 giveback shrank to 237.4M — a light-volume pullback after heavier-volume advances, with 7/27 closing at its high (14148.73). The ten sessions show perfect up/down alternation (all four prior down days were each followed by up days), and with a ~2.3% average absolute daily move, a >1% rebound toward the 13570/13842 resistance zone is the higher-probability next session.
prediction.market_analysis: A strong_up session would confirm that the two-week distribution after the 7/21 peak has been digested and that the 13068-13285 floor holds, implying a broad risk-on day for A-shares: high-beta Shenzhen growth sectors — semiconductors and tech hardware, NEV/battery chains, and ChiNext names that amplify 399001 — should lead alongside brokers, while defensives (banks, utilities, dividend plays) likely lag. First resistance sits at 13570 (8/03 high), then the 13842-13941 supply zone; clearing it opens a retest of 14150-14265, whereas failure would keep the index chopping in the 13068-14265 range with fast sector rotation. Positioning under this view favors oversold, volume-leading growth names over defensive exposure, with any early dip toward the 13400 area attractive given the higher-low structure and the market's demonstrated tendency to snap back violently (three of five up days exceeded +1.1%, including +2.72% and +2.21%).
